entries.exactPassage: Key idea: Themba's four streams became three. The online store disappeared overnight — not because he did anything wrong, but because the platform changed its rules. He had no control. The only streams that survived were the ones he owned — his client relationships, his savings. Control matters more than count. Five dependent streams are not better than two you own.
entries.concern: The statement that only owned streams survived contradicts the surviving part-time job shown in the table.
entries.proposedWording: The online store closed after the platform changed its rules. His part-time job, tutoring and savings interest survived, with different vulnerabilities and degrees of agency. Control matters alongside diversification, income needs and the risks that remain.
entries.implementationImpact: Separate owner-reviewed learner-source proposal only. No wording, response key, activity or canonical block is changed now.

entries.exactPassage: "That control matters more than count. The online store scored a 3 — I depended on the platform. The tutoring scores a 4 — I own the client relationships. The savings interest scores a 5 — no one can take it. I am shifting toward higher control. Building the tutoring. Letting go of platform-dependent income. It means earning less now. But what I earn, I keep. What I keep, no one can take."
entries.concern: Ownership and a high agency score do not make clients, rates, savings institutions or payments impossible to interrupt. The absolute no-one-can-take-it wording can be mistaken for a financial guarantee.
entries.proposedWording: I have more influence over my tutoring relationships than over the platform’s rules. My savings are mine, but rates, access and other risks still need checking. I am building agency while considering the income I need now.
entries.implementationImpact: Separate owner-reviewed learner-source proposal only. No wording, response key, activity or canonical block is changed now.

entries.exactPassage: Zola said accountability saved her. Name TWO people you will tell about this plan. Telling them creates the productive embarrassment that keeps you going.
entries.concern: Accountability is useful, but productive embarrassment should not become coerced disclosure or pressure to continue an unsuitable plan. The later text intensifies this into making quitting embarrassing.
entries.proposedWording: Choose two suitable people you could ask for willing, respectful follow-up on a feasible milestone. Agree what to share and review the plan honestly if it needs to change or stop.
entries.implementationImpact: Separate participation-wording review including the related Deepening Insight; no new compulsory activity or response field. A local task-specific safeguard is already in the draft.

entries.exactPassage: This week, delegate ONE task you usually do yourself. Let someone else do it. Do not check. Do not correct. Just observe. Write down: What happened? How did it feel? What did you learn about yourself?
entries.concern: The blanket Do not check or correct instruction can be copied for care, medicine, hazardous tools or essential responsibilities that require competent checking.
entries.proposedWording: Choose an agreed low-risk, reversible task with a willing suitable person. Keep necessary safety and quality checks. If no suitable task or person is available, record that and review the plan with the educator instead of carrying out an unsafe experiment.
entries.implementationImpact: Separate source safeguard; preserve existing task evidence identities. Local later-work guidance supplies this specific safeguard now.

entries.concern: Fixed predictable income, all risk, unlimited potential and limited control are simplified tendencies rather than universal conditions of employment or entrepreneurship.
entries.proposedWording: Label the comparison as possible tendencies. Actual security, control, hours, benefits, growth and income vary by role, enterprise, market, legal conditions and resources. Use current circumstances to reason about a fit.
